searches_tried: pipeline/comps.py: 'sterling fiddle tablespoons' (none), 'silver tablespoons pair' (Leski/Noble colonial Australian only, not comparable, excluded), 'victorian silver spoons', 'sterling tablespoons' (none), 'fiddle pattern', 'crested silver spoons' (none); work/comps.py 'silver tablespoons' (none). No true Australian competitive-room comp for plain Victorian London fiddle tablespoons in the databases. Colonial Australian silver hits (Leski $800-$5,500) are different items (maker marks by colonial silversmiths) and were excluded; worth noting only if the maker mark proves colonial, which the full English hallmarks make unlikely. No rate used; all figures as printed.
chrome_hint: eBay AU sold + Terapeak: 'sterling silver fiddle pattern tablespoons pair London Victorian' and 'antique sterling silver tablespoons pair crested', filter Sold, last 12 months; also eBay UK sold same terms (convert GBP to AUD). Auction houses: Leski, Noble Numismatics, Theodore Bruce, Mossgreen/Lawsons, The-Saleroom and LiveAuctioneers 'pair silver fiddle tablespoons London' (check 'sold'). Also check current silver spot (AUD per oz) to value ~140 g sterling as melt, and note that crested fiddle tablespoons often sell near weight in UK rooms.
viewing_check: Photograph both bowls' backs and the full hallmark row on each spoon in sharp macro: confirm maker mark (WE or other), date letter and city (London vs Exeter, Dublin, Edinburgh), duty mark, and weigh the pair if possible. Check for the crest engraving (a notable family or Australian colonial association would add value), bowl wear or thinning, and any splits.
